correctness.rationale: Direct MGF factorization proves q>=1/4 ordering. For q<1/4 the tilt-mean ratio increases strictly from 4q to 2, forcing I_q-I_0 to rise then fall, hence at most one positive intersection. Bounded-jump Legendre inversion proves exactly one speed reversal including saturation. The q_c polynomial follows by eliminating the v=1 optimizing tilt. Endpoint q=1, R->1 and R->infinity and strictness were checked. All algebraic proof steps are shown in RESULT.md; 8,000 reproducible supplementary checks from verify.py succeeded. Finite checks alone are not proofs.

value.rationale: This is a full sharp phase diagram for a biologically interpretable dispersal tradeoff: rare twice-long jumps have lower small-growth invasion speed despite a higher maximal travel step, yet win once reproduction becomes large enough. It identifies a distinct nontrivial boundary q_c deciding whether the switch occurs before or after the local kernel's support-limited speed ceiling. The exact threshold distinguishes genuinely different population-front regimes beyond an isolated numeric example. It is not a claim about stochastic or empirical spread.
